newsitem.title: USA: Clinton leads Dole by 14 points in California.
newsitem.headline: Clinton leads Dole by 14 points in California.

text.p: President Bill Clinton leads Republican challenger Bob Dole by a solid 14 points in California just days away from Tuesday's election, according to a poll published on Friday.
The San Francisco Examiner newspaper's poll showed Clinton with the support of 49 percent of the state's likely voters while 35 percent were for Dole.
The poll was a blow to Dole's chances in California, the most populous U.S. state with the largest number of electoral votes, 54, almost a third of the total needed to win the presidency.
Dole had made an all-out push to capture the state.
The Examiner poll also found that Clinton was leading in traditionally Republican strongholds -- by four points in San Diego County and six points in California's Central Valley.
On Thursday, the independent Field Institute released a poll that showed Clinton with a commanding 18-point lead over Dole in California.
Reform Party candidate Ross Perot captured six percent in the new Examiner poll, while the Green Party's Ralph Nader took two percent. Eight percent were still undecided.

The Examiner poll of 839 likely California voters, by Washington-based Mason-Dixon Media/Political Research, was undertaken Oct. 28-30, and has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.5 percentage points, the newspaper said.
